activity.title: 36 hours in LA. Maybe 5 hours of sleep. By the end of the weekend, we placed 2nd overall at LA Hacks and won the Fetch.ai Best Use of ASI:One prize. We built around a simple but urgent reality: Disasters like building collapses don’t just trap people, they create conditions where safely reaching those in need becomes the biggest challenge. We built RIIS, a system designed for the moments when responders can’t safely enter yet. An autonomous rover navigates unstable environments, detects survivors, establishes voice contact, and generates structured triage reports using a multi agent AI pipeline. We also reconstruct the entire scene in 3D using Gaussian Splatting, so responders can understand and plan before ever stepping inside. Last weekend, I participated in DiamondHacks 2026, where Aaditya Pillai , Krish Kankure , Varun Sinha , and I built LungIQ: a project focused on improving lung health analysis with an interactive AI dashboard. We ended up winning the Health track, which was a great validation of our team's effort and the way we executed our project idea. Over a short time, we worked on: • building an end-to-end pipeline for analyzing lung-related data • integrating machine learning models into a usable interface • thinking through how this could be applied in real-world healthcare settings We learned a lot from this hackathon, especially about building fast, iterating quickly, and communicating technical ideas clearly. Huge thanks to ACM at UC San Diego for hosting this hackathon! Check out our project here: https://lnkd.in/enERZmJr ...more ...more

What if robot footage could become more than video? Proud to share that our team won 2nd place at LA Hacks and Fetch.ai ’s Best Use of ASI:One award with RIIS, a project at the intersection of robotics, 3D reconstruction, and VR. After an earthquake collapse, finding survivors is only part of the challenge. Reaching them safely and quickly is just as critical. RIIS sends an autonomous rover into the rubble before responders enter. It detects survivors, initiates voice contact, generates AI-powered triage reports, and reconstructs the scene in 3D using Gaussian Splatting. Responders can then explore that reconstruction in VR before stepping inside. What started as a weekend build has pushed us toward a bigger question: how can spatial AI turn real-world environments into live, reliable, and interactive 3D experiences that teams can deploy, explore, and act on at scale? If you’re working on 3D reconstruction, spatial AI, robotics, or AR/VR, I’d love to connect and talk. Grateful to my teammates Krish Kankure , Aaditya Pillai , and Varun Sinha , and to LA Hacks for an incredible experience. This is just the start.

Disappointed to announce I wore the same shirt at LA Hacks as I did at DiamondHacks . However, happy to announce we placed 2nd overall and won the Fetch.ai Best Use of ASI:One prize. We built RIIS. When a building collapses, survival rates drop with every passing minute, not because rescue is impossible, but because care can't reach the patient in time. The barrier isn't medical capability. It's access. RIIS is a ground robot that enters collapsed structures ahead of human responders, streaming live video to a command dashboard where YOLOv8 runs in real time, drawing skeleton overlays on any survivors it detects. From there a four-agent AI pipeline kicks in automatically. Triage assessment gets generated using ASI-1 Mini, the rover speaks to the patient in their native language via ElevenLabs , and the scene gets reconstructed in 3D so incident commanders can walk through it in VR before anyone steps inside. Really proud of what we built with Krish Kankure , Aaditya Pillai , and Srinivas Sriram . Demo Video: https://lnkd.in/g3WrPzPz Devpost: https://lnkd.in/gXMTBTrc Github: https://lnkd.in/gGsyzYZM
